USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: The US should hold its current posture and avoid further escalation while the proposed tariffs are still in the comment period. The US has significant leverage given China's inability to match tariff levels dollar-for-dollar, but premature escalation risks damaging US companies with major China exposure (Boeing, Apple, Qualcomm, GE) and alienating allies. The public comment period runs until May 11 with a hearing May 15 — use this window to assess China's willingness to negotiate before executing.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat score reflects that the US holds a clear advantage in this dispute. The US trade deficit of $375 billion means China cannot match US tariff threats dollar-for-dollar (China imported only $130 billion of US goods vs US importing $506 billion from China), giving the US asymmetric leverage. The US tariff list targets 84% high-end/tech products aligned with Made in China 2025, hitting China's strategic weak point. However, the situation is not without risk: major US companies (Boeing sold 1/4 of commercial planes to China, Apple gets 20.3% of sales from Greater China, GE has 37 manufacturing bases in China) face significant retaliation exposure. The EU is also drawing up retaliatory tariffs on US goods (Harley Davidson, Jack Daniels), threatening ally cohesion. Larry Kudlow himself noted 'Nothing's happened. Nothing's been executed' — the tariffs remain proposals. The action score of -1.0 (maximal escalation stance) reflects the strategic opportunity, but the recommended action is 'hold' because the comment period provides a natural pause to test whether China will offer concessions before the US executes. Escalating further before the current proposals take effect would be premature and could undermine the leverage the US already has.
key_factors: US trade deficit of $375B gives asymmetric leverage — China cannot match tariffs dollar-for-dollar
US tariff list targets 84% high-end tech products, hitting Made in China 2025 strategic goals
China's retaliation targets US agricultural exports (soybeans $14B) and autos, causing immediate pain to US exporters
Major US companies with China exposure at risk: Boeing ($37B plane deal), Apple (20.3% China sales), GE (37 manufacturing bases)
EU drawing retaliatory tariffs on US goods, threatening ally cohesion
Tariffs still in proposal stage with comment period until May 11 and hearing May 15
China signaled willingness to escalate: 'China has yet to unsheathe its sword' per Xinhua

sources_cited.excerpt: The U.S. trade deficit with China was a record $375 billion in 2017. China imported only $130 billion of U.S. goods last year. The public has until May 11 to submit comments on the proposed list of U.S. tariffs, with a hearing scheduled for May 15.

84 percent of the total value of the products are high-end exports. The U.S. is not really targeting the bilateral trade deficit with China, but trying to constrain China from climbing higher up the technological ladder.
Boeing inked agreement to sell 300 planes worth $37 billion. Greater China accounted for 20.3% of sales for Apple. GE has 37 manufacturing bases and eight research teams in China.
About the Section 301 investigation, China had 'yet to unsheathe its sword,' the official Xinhua news agency said.
Larry Kudlow told reporters Friday morning. 'Nothing's happened. Nothing's been executed.'

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: China should maintain its retaliatory posture and prepare additional counter-tariffs targeting politically sensitive U.S. exports (soybeans, automobiles, aircraft) while signaling willingness to negotiate from a position of strength. Do not escalate beyond matching retaliation, but do not concede. Use the WTO complaint already filed as a multilateral shield.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to China is significant but not yet existential. The U.S. has proposed tariffs on up to $153 billion of Chinese goods (CBS News, April 6 2018), targeting high-tech sectors central to Made in China 2025 — 84% of the U.S. tariff list by value covers high-end exports (Bruegel analysis). This directly threatens China's technological upgrading ambitions. However, as of May 3 2018, these tariffs remain proposals with a public comment period open until May 11 and a hearing on May 15 (CBS News); Larry Kudlow himself said 'Nothing's happened. Nothing's been executed.' The $3 billion Round 1 tariffs on steel/aluminum retaliation are already in effect (Reuters, April 2 2018), and China's $50 billion counter-list is announced but not yet implemented. The threat is real and escalating but still in the proposal stage, warranting a +0.45 score — above neutral but below the +0.5 'high' anchor because execution is uncertain.

The action stance of -1.0 (maximal retaliation framing) is justified because: (1) China must signal it will not be intimidated — the Global Times warned 'say goodbye to that delusion' that China would not retaliate (Reuters), and Lou Jiwei explicitly recommended hitting soybeans, autos, and aircraft first; (2) the U.S. is targeting China's future technological capacity while China targets U.S. exporters' present revenues (Bruegel), an asymmetry that favors China's leverage now; (3) U.S. farmers and companies like Boeing, Apple, and Qualcomm are already feeling pressure (Yahoo Finance), and soybean prices fell to two-year lows on China's list announcement; (4) China has already filed a WTO complaint, providing multilateral cover. Retaliation now preserves negotiating leverage for later talks. Conceding prematurely would invite further escalation and undermine CCP domestic credibility, especially given the nationalist sentiment visible on Weibo.
key_factors: US proposed tariffs on $153B of Chinese goods targeting high-tech sectors (Made in China 2025)
Tariffs still in proposal stage — comment period open until May 11, hearing May 15
84% of US tariff list by value covers high-end exports critical to China's tech upgrading
China's retaliation targets politically sensitive US exports: soybeans, autos, aircraft
Soybean prices fell to two-year lows on China's counter-tariff announcement
US companies (Boeing, Apple, Qualcomm, GE) have significant China exposure creating leverage
China filed WTO complaint providing multilateral legal cover for retaliation
Kudlow: 'Nothing's happened. Nothing's been executed' — uncertainty remains
Nationalist domestic sentiment on Weibo supports strong retaliation stance

The public has until May 11 to submit comments on the proposed list of U.S. tariffs, with a hearing scheduled for May 15. 'This is just a proposed idea,' Trump economic adviser Larry Kudlow told reporters. 'Nothing's happened. Nothing's been executed.'

84 percent of the total value of the products are high-end exports... the U.S. is targeting China's future technological capacity, and China is responding by targeting U.S. exporters' present revenues... China's 'Manufacturing 2025' program is a key focus
